narrative:
The model determined that you have a 34% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability exceeded the bank's acceptance threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were your credit history, the status of your checking account, and the length of the loan you requested. Your credit history had the largest impact and pushed the decision toward denial. Having no credits or all paid worked against you because the bank sees this as limited evidence of reliable repayment behavior; only 1% of approved applicants share this profile, while most successful applicants have either existing paid credits or a critical credit history that demonstrates proven reliability.

Your checking account status was the second most important factor and actually helped your case. Holding 200 DM or more, or receiving salary into the account, is relatively uncommon (only about 10% of applicants), and the model viewed this positively compared with many approved borrowers who often show lower or negative balances.

The shorter nine-month duration you requested was the third key driver and also worked in your favor. Approved applicants typically request almost twice as long (19 months on average), so your modest timeframe signaled lower risk.

While these elements created an overall picture the model could not approve, you can strengthen future applications by building a longer track record of on-time payments to improve how your credit history is viewed. Consider reapplying once you have established more positive repayment references.
